name: AU Small Finance Bank Ltd
title: AU Small Finance Bank Ltd - 540611 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: AU SFB Q1 FY27 profit rose 37% YoY to INR796 cr, with NIM at 5.9% (+47 bps YoY) and deposits up 24% YoY.
summary.overview: AU Small Finance Bank reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR796 crore, up 37% YoY, driven by 41% core PPOP growth and a 47 bps YoY rise in NIM to 5.9%. Loans grew 23% YoY and deposits 24% YoY, both well ahead of private sector bank growth. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with slippages down 22% to INR798 crore and credit cost down 54 bps to 0.8%. Sequentially, NIM eased 7 bps and provisions rose 38% on seasonality, and an additional one-time INR23 crore provision was taken on unsecured products.

financial_highlights.change: Driven by business volumes and credit card issuance

segments.name: Retail secured (wheels, mortgages, gold loan)
segments.commentary: 67% of portfolio, grew 23% YoY and 4% QoQ. Wheels book INR48,600 crore (+28% YoY, +5% QoQ); gold loan INR4,500 crore (+130% YoY, +15% QoQ); mortgages +12% YoY, disbursements +28% YoY.

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: INR32,800 crore, up 34% YoY and 6% QoQ. Transaction banking and forex income up 46% YoY and 8% QoQ.

segments.name: Inclusive banking (MFI)
segments.commentary: Grew 15% YoY and 5% QoQ. Collection efficiency 99.5%; 96% of the book covered under CGFMU guarantee.

segments.name: Digital unsecured
segments.commentary: Grew 3% YoY and 7% QoQ. Personal loans +24% YoY and +19% QoQ from a low base; credit card growth marginal, with new card issuances crossing 1 lakh in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Cost to assets ratio expected to improve on a full-year basis, per management.
Management sees scope for improvement in opex and credit cost versus full FY26, which it says will take ROA to the guided range (target ~1.8%); CEO said the gap is about 10 bps.
No NIM guidance given; cost of funds has effectively bottomed, so the cost line is expected to be stable to slightly rising, with asset yields tracking mix.
Expects to add 100+ deposit branches this year (16 added in Q1).
ECL transition impact: management expects it to be neutral given low LGDs, but said quantification will come around end of Q3.
Long-term aspiration to grow at 2x to 2.5x India's nominal GDP growth.
capex_capacity: Added 16 deposit branches in Q1; on track for 100+ in FY27.
Gold loan distribution extended to 400+ existing branches in Q1, taking total to over 1,300 branches.
Gold loan rolled out on an AI-enabled origination platform; mobile version live and branch extension to be calibrated.
Technology spend close to INR1,000 crore, about 12-13% of opex.
Vehicle finance distribution strengthened in South, UP and newer eastern states.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth 24% YoY vs private sector 14%; loan growth 23% YoY vs private sector 17%.
Management flagged tight liquidity, heightened deposit competition and elevated rates.
FCNR rates raised to about 7.4-7.5% as US dollar leverage constrains customers; no specific FCNR target.
Savings account cost about 5.05% and term deposit cost about 7.25%.
Stable deposits (CASA, retail TDs, non-callable bulk TDs) at 79% of total deposits.
Credit cards: revolve book reduced after underwriting tightening ~18 months ago, depressing yields.
Gold loan: average ticket about INR2.5 lakh, majority below INR5 lakh, over 80% rural, portfolio IRR about 15.5%.
Renewable energy book (grew ~120%+ YoY) is lent to developers in KUSUM A/C projects of 2-5 MW, mainly Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and MP.

qa_highlights.question: Commercial banking slippage uptick QoQ and its nature?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said Q4 is seasonally strong, so YoY is the right comparison; commercial banking slippages are lower YoY and bank-level slippages improved about 150 bps. The QoQ uptick is in the SME book, which typically rises in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of ECL framework on steady-state credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is hard to quantify now. Models are being refined with external agencies, and Stage 3 provisions give comfort to cover incremental Stage 1 and 2 provisions. Management called the impact neutral given low LGDs; more clarity expected by end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Risk-adjusted yields and profitability of digital unsecured (credit cards and PL)?
qa_highlights.answer: Prince Tiwari said these are newer businesses and product-level risk-adjusted metrics are not yet meaningful. Credit cards are loss-making and PL is around breakeven, per management. Gaurav Jain said the card yield is subdued because the revolve book fell after underwriting tightening.

qa_highlights.question: NIM trajectory for the next two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain declined to give directional NIM guidance. Cost of funds has bottomed, with savings and deposit rates raised, so the cost line should be stable to slightly up depending on rates.

qa_highlights.question: MFI growth sustainability and CV credit environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said the industry is recovering after degrowth and MFIN projects 17-18% growth. Q1 collection efficiency is 99.5%, and vehicle distribution has expanded in South, UP and East with no abnormal stress seen.

qa_highlights.question: Which CD ratio is used internally and NSFR range?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said CD ratio ex-refinance is about 80% and is the internal measure. Prince Tiwari said the LCR range is about 115-120% and NSFR about 105-115%.

qa_highlights.question: ROA target of 1.8% and whether NIM is stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said there is no NIM guidance; opex and credit cost have room to improve versus FY26. Sanjay Agarwal said the bank is about 10 bps short of the target, with other income and credit cost each contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Employee count decline and MFI credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said May was the first month of manpower reduction, and back-end hiring has stopped because of AI. Front-end hiring continues for new geographies. On MFI, the 3% credit cost view is no longer the right optics; guarantee cost is now built in, so about 2.5% is possible.

risks_watch: ECL transition: cost and timing not yet quantified; management says more detail by end of Q3.
Credit card and PL profitability remain immature; the card book is loss-making.
NIM direction not guided; cost of funds stable to rising in a tight liquidity market.
CGFMU claim recovery: claims for FY26 pool expected to be lodged by end Q2 and realised around December; GNPA coverage is slightly lower than SMA coverage.
Cost to assets is 4.0% versus 3.9% last year; opex growth of 26% YoY is above income growth.
Management succession and the new Deputy CEO elevation are in focus.
One-time INR23 crore provision from tighter norms on unsecured products.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and the ROA path, but guarded on NIM, ECL and product-level profitability, where management repeatedly deferred to later quarters. Management was open on the employee count decline and the MFI guarantee model.
key_quotes: Deposits growth remained robust at 24% year-on-year, significantly ahead of the estimated private sector banking deposit growth of 14%.
So give us some time and you will see the underlying profit pools emerging in our unsecured businesses over time.
It's a very, very granular book.
